intro.title: Cookie-Based Auth Flow
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React application that simulates a cookie-based authentication flow. You will learn how to manage user login and logout states, and conditionally render content based on whether a user is authenticated. The core programming concepts used are React state management with the useState hook and conditional rendering. You will work with JSX for the user interface and handle basic click events to update the application's state. This hands-on project will help you understand how authentication status can control what users see in a web application.
intro.usecase: Cookie-based authentication is the foundation of session management in countless web applications. When you log into platforms like GitHub, Notion, or banking dashboards, your browser stores an authentication cookie that keeps you logged in across page refreshes and navigation. As a developer, implementing this flow means creating login forms that securely exchange credentials for cookies, protecting user dashboards and admin panels from unauthorized access. This pattern is essential for any application requiring persistent user sessions without exposing tokens in client-side JavaScript.
